General Relativity and Spacetime Curvature

1. The Geometrization of Gravitation

Albert Einstein's general theory of relativity establishes that spacetime curvature is directly coupled to energy-momentum distribution.

Einstein Field Equations with Cosmological Constant:
Gμν + Λ gμν = (8 π G / c4) Tμν

Here, Gμν is the Einstein tensor, defined in terms of the Ricci curvature tensor Rμν and Ricci scalar R:

Gμν = Rμν - (1 / 2) R gμν

2. The Schwarzschild Vacuum Metric

Outside a spherically symmetric, static mass M, the line element in spherical coordinates (t, r, θ, φ) is:

ds2 = -(1 - 2GM / (c2 r)) c2 dt2 + (1 - 2GM / (c2 r))-1 dr2 + r2 (dθ2 + sin2θ dφ2)

The Schwarzschild radius rs = 2GM / c2 defines the event horizon of a non-rotating black hole.
